payload.text:
Saya ingin membuat website untuk pemesanan Pelayanan General Service, Dengan main menu: Mess, KRP, dan Maintenance. sub menu Dashboard dan Request

Dalam sub Menu Request mess terdapat pilihan mess Banjarbaru, Batu Butok, Long Ikis dan Tanjung serta kolom isian Nama tamu, Jumlah kamar, nama pemesan, fungsi, Nomer Handphone Tamu, tanggal check in dan out (ketika di klik muncul kalender tanggal yang akan dipilih).

Dalam sub Menu Request KRP terdapat kolom isian, Nama penumpang, jumlah penumpang, fungsi, nomer handphone penumpang, tanggal berangkat dan pulang (ketika di klik muncul kalender tanggal yang akan dipilih), jam berangkat dan pulang(ketika di klik muncul jam yang akan dipilih). ada pilihan tombol pulang pergi? (ketika diklik maka kolom tanggal pulang dan jam pulang baru muncul)

Dalam sub menu Request maintenance terdapat Pemilihan kategori pekerjaan yaitu Fasilitas Umum, Electrical maintenance, Civil Maintenance, AC Maintenance, dan House Keeping serta kolom isian, nama pemesan, fungsi, nome handphone pemesan, tanggal, dan detail pekerjaan. 

Dalam sub Menu Dashboard terdapat Card interaktif (Requested, on Progress, pending, close) dan didalamnya terdapat total pekerjaan masing-masing. Ketika kita klik salah satu card maka akan muncul detail pekerjaan seperti tanggal pekerjaan, kategori pekerjaan, nama pemesan, dan detail pekerjaan serta status pekerjaan yang dapat diklik dan diubah statusnya.

**Defining Service Structure**

I'm currently structuring the booking website. I've begun defining the key service areas: Mess, KRP (Transport), and Maintenance. I'm focusing on their core sub-menus – Dashboard and Request. Specifically, I'm now outlining the "Mess Request" form fields, including Location (Banjarbaru, etc.), Guest Name, and Number. I'm moving toward detailing the requirements of these sections.


**Detailing Request Forms**

I'm now detailing the form fields for each request type. "Mess Request" includes Room details, Requester Name, and Check-in/Check-out dates. "KRP Request" includes Passenger info and trip details. "Maintenance Request" will have category, requester, and work details. I'm also planning the shared dashboard components with interactive status cards.


**Refining UI Structure**

I'm now refining the UI. I've designed a dynamic `RequestForm` component, with corresponding TypeScript interfaces, selection constants, and (simulated) state management. I'm focusing on a clean, professional UI with a corporate color palette, incorporating mobile responsiveness with a collapsible sidebar. I'm also planning real-time status updates for the dashboard. Finally, I've re-structured the UI so that users choose a Service Type (Main Menu) and can then switch between Dashboard and Request.

**Refining the Portal Design**

I'm currently focused on simplifying the "General Service" portal. The initial plan involves streamlining the navigation to three core menus: "Mess," "KRP," and "Maintenance." Each of these will house the essential sub-menus "Dashboard" and "Request". Further improvements have been planned to eliminate unnecessary elements.


**Streamlining Core Portal Functions**

I've just been reviewing the recent feedback and restructuring the "App.tsx" file. I'm focusing on the state management for the three core services and their sub-menus. The plan involves removing the header buttons. The Desktop Sidebar and Mobile Bottom Nav will remain. I'm maintaining the existing DashboardView and forms, ensuring that they fit the new, compact design.


**Prioritizing UI for Compactness**

I'm now prioritizing a streamlined UI for mobile. My current approach involves making the service selection (Mess, KRP, Maintenance) the primary choice through the Sidebar or Bottom Nav. I'm planning to introduce a toggle within the main view for switching between Dashboard and Request views for each service. I'm keeping the desktop header minimal, removing the search, bell, and new request options. The mobile bottom nav will just have service icons.


**Implementing Tab Navigation**

I'm now integrating a tab navigation bar within the main content area for switching between "Dashboard" and "Request" views. This replaces the toggle I was considering earlier. I'm removing all header actions, and the bottom nav will only show service icons (Mess, KRP, Maintenance). I'm focusing on refining `App.tsx` layout and polishing `DashboardView.tsx`, ensuring dark mode compatibility and mobile responsiveness. The `activeService` and `activeSubMenu` states in `App.tsx` will handle the tab switching, which is now the core navigation model.

**Analyzing Form Alignment**

I'm currently focused on pinpointing the root cause of the misalignment between "Tanggal Berangkat" and "Jam Berangkat" in the KRP request form. My initial hypothesis is that varying label lengths are the culprit, but I am exploring this further and testing several ideas.


**Refining Grid and Labels**

I'm now zeroing in on the grid structure within `KRPRequestForm.tsx` to tackle the column misalignment. My current plan involves carefully examining the spacing within the grid layout, with a focus on ensuring date and time input fields have consistent widths. Also, I'm considering label adjustments: shortening "Tanggal Berangkat" to "Tgl. Berangkat" and "Jam Berangkat" to "Jam" to see if that streamlines the visual flow and reduces any spacing issues. My goal is to maintain that compact, tidy design they're after.


**Aligning Component Heights**

I'm now directing my focus towards the height discrepancies between the "Jam Berangkat" and "Tanggal Berangkat" input fields. I'm going to look into `inputClasses` and containers to ensure consistent heights and margins. I suspect browser defaults for date/time inputs might be the issue, and I'll ensure the "Pulang Pergi" toggle is well-integrated. Additionally, I plan to audit `KRPRequestForm.tsx`, `MessRequestForm.tsx`, and `MaintenanceRequestForm.tsx` to fix column alignment inconsistencies. Specifically for `KRPRequestForm.tsx`, consistent heights for `departureDate`, `departureTime`, and the `isRoundTrip` section are critical. I also noticed the labels are "TANGGAL BERANGKAT" and "JAM BERANGKAT" in the image.
